title: Pinned real Ribasim clock-aligned priority allocation followed by physical realization shortfall

relation_to_19e.controlled_change: solver.saveat changes from 3600 s to 86400 s so the output/save boundary is aligned with allocation.dt=86400 s.

purpose: Recover the originally intended scientific mechanism under configuration semantics that actually provide one allocation solve for the one-day physical window. This isolates management priority allocation followed by physical source-state realization from the saveat-driven reallocation discovered by DUMMY-19E.

independent_continuous_reference.ode: A dh/dtau = 32 * (1 - phi(h-0.99)), tau in days, with a single allocation target fixed for the one-day window.
independent_continuous_reference.ledger: 32 m3 fixed inflow = physical UserDemand supply + Basin storage gain.

hypotheses: Clock alignment produces one effective allocation solve for the one-day window.
Root-first allocation stays 32/0 m3/day throughout the physical window; external-first stays 12/20 m3/day.
The common physical factor reduces only already allocated links.
Root-first therefore physically supplies approximately 16.0192 m3 to root and zero to external demand.
External-first physically supplies approximately 6.00719 m3 root and 10.01199 m3 external.
Both priority cases have the same total physical supply, final Basin level and storage gain because their total allocated target is identical.
Allocated-but-unsupplied water remains in Basin storage.
The difference between DUMMY-19E and DUMMY-19E2 is clock configuration, not a change to the management-versus-realization hypothesis.
forbidden: no changing any expected physical value or tolerance after execution
no interpreting DUMMY-19E2 as repairing or qualifying the failed DUMMY-19E configuration
no claim that solver.saveat should be a management clock
